candidates.location_hint: The flex container holding the main content area and the sidebar panel
candidates.why: Visual reordering via CSS likely diverges from the natural DOM tab sequence, which could disorient keyboard users expecting focus to follow the layout.

candidates.location_hint: The target element referenced by the skip link at the top of the page
candidates.why: Standard divs are not natively focusable, so activating the skip link may scroll to the element without moving keyboard focus to it.

candidates.location_hint: The focus outline style applied to links inside the left sidebar navigation panel
candidates.why: The light outline color against the near-white sidebar background may fall below the minimum contrast threshold required for visible focus states.

candidates.location_hint: The floating action button in the bottom-right corner with an explicit positive tab index value
candidates.why: Positive tab indices force elements into the early tab sequence, potentially placing this button before the skip link and main navigation, breaking logical focus flow.

candidates.location_hint: The heading structure inside the sidebar panel versus the main content area
candidates.why: While headings appear present, verifying that landmark regions and their associated headings maintain a logical, non-skipping hierarchy for screen reader navigation is worth a quick check.
